title: After hours at 18th and Vine and with Joe Turner
summary: Musicians met in the street at 18th and Vine and Durham played after hours with Joe Turner and Jo Jones, paid in money stuffed in his guitar.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: It's one thing about Kansas City that nobody never mentioned. After all the jobs was over, all the musicians would meet right on 18th and Vine, and the meeting place was right in the middle of the street.
And Ben Webster used to get --
So they all used to meet in the middle of the street.

Later, after -- that was the third job, because they all would leave one job around 2:00 or 3:00 or 4:00, and go to another job, you see. When I'd get off around 3:00 or 4:00 at the Cherry Blossom or any of those places, I'd go down to Piney Brown's or down there where Joe Turner was bartending. When I'd walk in, I'd have my guitar throwed across my neck.
The guitar, I had it swinging on my back.

Then I'd go there and I'd jump up on the stage there and sit up on the bar and get the guitar, and Joe Turner would wipe his hands, and he'd come there and he'd sing, see, and Joe Turner would sing and Jo Jones would have his snare drum, he'd come in -- no, with his sock cymbal, and it'd be about three of us. And that was another job. We used to work there until about 7:00 the next morning.

And he didn't have to pay us anything, because when I'd come out, money'd be sticking all up -- rolled up and stuck into the guitar, and put it in Joe Turner's pocket and that's where I first met him, and we used to play like that.
